newsitem.title: USA: Newmont 1997 gold production on target.
newsitem.headline: Newmont 1997 gold production on target.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp said Monday it is on target to produce 2.6 million ounces of gold in 1997 at a total cash cost of under $200 per ounce.
The company reported first quarter earnings of $20.4 million compared with $10.7 million a year ago.
The company said 91-percent owned Newmont Gold Co, owner of Newmont Mining's operating assets, earned $22.6 million compared to $11.8 million in 1996's initial quarter.
Earnings per share nearly doubled to $0.21 from $0.11 in 1996 as total equity gold production rose 37 percent and total cash costs per ounce of production were reduced 17 percent.
"It was an outstanding quarter in which every operation exceeded its production target and achieved significantly lower costs," said chief executive Ronald Cambre.

"As an essentially unhedged company, the gain came despite a $48 drop in our realized gold price, and underscores the ... potential earnings impact our shareholders can expect from appreciating gold prices."

First quarter gold production rose to 621,800 equity ounces from 452,700 ounces, as total cash costs, including royalty payments, fell to $192 per equity ounce from $230. The company said it realized $354 per ounce of gold sold.
That compares to $402 an ounce in the 1996 quarter.

Newmont said its Carlin, Nev., operations produced 420,600 ounces of gold in the quarter, a 17 percent increase from the prior year's 359,300 ounces. Total cash costs dropped to $212 per ounce from $255 a year earlier. While record snow fall and downtime at the roaster limited production a year ago, productivity improved significantly in 1997.
Carlin operations are expected to produce approximately 1.8 million ounces of gold in 1997 with further cost reductions in subsequent quarters, the company said.

The company said the Minera Yanacocha in Peru has increased its production forecast for 1997 to 900,000 ounces reflecting development of a fourth mine, Cerro Yanacocha Norte, later in the year. Newmont's equity interest in this production would be 452,400 ounces, it noted.
The company said its newest project, Minahasa Raya in Indonesia, should produce over 160,000 ounces this year. In the first quarter, Minasha Raya produced 39,000 ounces.
Newmmont said the Zarafshan-Newmont project in Uzbekistan produced 109,400 ounces of gold in the first quarter compared to 51,400 for the same period a year ago.
The company said said delays in the approvals for the Batu Hijau project, the large copper/gold deposit in Indonesia, could hurt the development of the project.
It said the Indonesian government has not yet issued the construction permit nor approved the participation of Newmont's partner, Sumitomo Corp.
Newmont said it had expected both approvals in the first quarter. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
